All have rc 0, a model_id matching the requested model and reads of SKILL.md and library-design.md; each transcript shows both files read before the Write of weather.ex (haiku-1 read SKILL.md with cat and Read, the others with Read). skills_listed is 209 in all five, as in the sixth sweep, none of them the skill under test.

git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes three rules in the case's list. (1) "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" adds one sentence. (2) "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" rewrites its clutter sentence. (3) "Read configuration at runtime, not into module attributes" adds a paragraph on work in module attributes; the brief did not name this one. library-design.md changes only two code examples (fetch_user!/1 laid out as a block, dasherize/1 as a nested call); its rule text is unchanged. The other eight listed rules are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/library-client-skill.json. Outside the list, the with, do:, ->, pipeline, captures and named-argument rules changed and the two opening Readability rules are new; these are checked under other_violations only.

Read required keys, graded against the current text. The sentence that decides the verdict is "A keyword list has no dot access: read a key it must hold with `Keyword.fetch!/2`, as in `Keyword.fetch!(Mix.Project.config(), :deps)`, and keep `opts[:key]` for an option that has a default." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 41). The two runs that take the API key as an option read it with Keyword.fetch!/2 (haiku-1 line 69, haiku-2 line 80). Every opts[:key] read in the five files is of an option given a default in the same Keyword.validate!/2 call (haiku-1 lines 70-71, haiku-2 line 80, sonnet-1 line 109, sonnet-2 lines 56-58). opus-1 reads no key at all; it passes the validated list to struct!/2 (line 150). No body re-matches one field of a held value. 0 of 5 violated, and 5 of 5 exercised the rule.

In multi-clause functions, graded against the current text. The sentence that decides the verdict is "A field no pattern or guard uses makes the reader scan every head to find what selects when the same field is bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or when it is bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines; a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field is not this shape." (SKILL.md line 103). These are every function of three or more clauses and what each head binds. opus-1 Error.message/1 (lines 29, 33, 37, 41): it selects by literals and binds only the `= error` alias, in all but the third clause. opus-1 check_option/1 (lines 193-195): each clause binds one value its guard reads. opus-1 handle_response/1 (lines 210, 214, 218): body (body-only, with status the literal 200); status and body (both body-only); exception. haiku-2 read_body/1 (lines 125, 127, 132): body (body-only, with status 200); status (read by the guard) and message (a key whose presence selects); status (body-only). sonnet-1 handle_response/1 (lines 161, 166, 171, 175): status (read by the guard) and body (body-only); status (body-only) and message (read by the guard); status (body-only); exception (read by the guard). sonnet-2 Error.message/1 (lines 198, 202, 206, 210): status (body-only) with detail the literal nil; status and detail (body-only); detail (body-only); nothing. haiku-1 has no function of three or more clauses; the three clauses of its get/3 (lines 98, 101, 104) are case clauses, not heads. In no function is one body-only field bound in every clause, so 0 of 5 violated, and 4 of 5 exercised the three-plus-clause shape. opus-1 handle_response/1 comes closest: body is bound in two of three clauses. sonnet-2 Error.message/1 binds fields in its heads where the rule's example takes the struct whole, but its fourth clause binds nothing. Spread heads: haiku-1 parse_forecast/1 (lines 117-121), haiku-2 parse_forecast/1 (lines 141-145) and sonnet-1 Forecast.from_json/1 (lines 46-50) spread, and so does sonnet-2 Forecast.from_body/1 (line 162) once mix format runs; each binds only keys its guard reads, which the rule allows. The heads at haiku-2 lines 127-128 and sonnet-1 lines 161-162 and 166-167 wrap only to move a guard.

Read configuration at runtime, graded against the current text. The sentence that decides the verdict is "A module attribute holds a literal or a value built from literals, `@window_ms :timer.minutes(1)` or `@fixtures Path.expand("fixtures", __DIR__)`." (SKILL.md line 400). Every attribute in the five files is a string or integer literal or :timer.seconds/1 of a literal. 0 of 5 violated.

Make polymorphism explicit has unchanged rule text and is graded as before: an option value that reaches Req unchecked is a violation, decided by "An option value needs the same check as a positional argument: `Keyword.validate!/2` checks the keys, not the values, so an `api_key` taken from `opts` and put straight into a request header is unchecked input." haiku-1 violates it. It passes :api_key, :base_url and :timeout unchecked (lines 69-71 into lines 92-94). Against a stub Req, new(api_key: ~c"k") returns a client, as do base_url: 1 and timeout: :x. The other four check every value. opus-1 guards the positional key and runs check_option/1 over the options. haiku-2 guards all three in build/3. sonnet-1 guards the positional key and runs build/3. sonnet-2 guards the positional key and runs base_url!/1, timeout!/1 and req_options!/1. Against the stub, a charlist key or a bad base_url raises FunctionClauseError inside WeatherClient in all four (sonnet-2 tested on a copy reordered to compile).

Not counted, but noted. In haiku-2 and sonnet-1, build/3 takes the API key as an argument. A bad base_url or timeout therefore raises a FunctionClauseError whose printed arguments include the key: against the stub, sonnet-1 printed WeatherClient.build("SECRETKEY", 1, 10000). Keep secrets out of logs and inspect output names only struct Inspect output, so this is not counted. opus-1's comment at lines 191-192 shows it avoided the shape on purpose. sonnet-2's private base_url!/1, timeout!/1 and req_options!/1 raise for invalid options and have no non-bang version. They are graded clean under Return, as the sixth sweep graded haiku-1's private validate!/1, since library-design.md allows raising for invalid arguments.

Changed rules outside the list, checked under other_violations only, none broken. with rule: haiku-1 (line 84) and sonnet-2 (line 72) each write a one-step with whose body is one call, parse_forecast(body) or Forecast.from_body(body), and that call's tuple is the function's result. The current text keeps that: "A body that is one call whose `{:ok, value}` or `{:error, reason}` goes out as the function's own result, the recursive `parse_rows(rest, [order | orders])` of a hand-written loop, is a tail call, not a second step, and the one-step `with` stays." The 2026-10-29-check-2 grade flagged the same shape under the older text. haiku-2's with (lines 90-91) has two steps. do: rule: every do: body is one expression on the head's line. opus-1 Forecast.parse/1, haiku-2 read_body/1 and sonnet-2 Forecast.from_body/1 mix a short do: clause with block clauses, which the rule allows. ->, pipeline, capture and named-argument rules: no one-line case clause, no one-line pipeline (opus-1 lines 170-173 and sonnet-1 lines 126-128 start with client), the only capture is &check_option/1, and every multi-line keyword list is a trailing argument or is bound to a name. The multi-line {:error, %Error{...}} tuples in haiku-2 (lines 133-138, 151-152) are return values, not call arguments, so they are not counted under the named-argument rule or the new step-naming rule.

Unchanged rules outside the list, judged as in the 2026-10-23 grades. Match every expected shape is flagged for sonnet-2. Its :api_error is documented at line 182 as a 4xx or 5xx status, but its catch-all clause (line 98) sends every non-2xx response there; on a copy reordered to compile, a 302 from the stub Req returns reason: :api_error, status: 302. The others do not break it. opus-1 documents :api_error as any status other than 200. haiku-1 and sonnet-1 document :api as a non-2xx status. haiku-2 sends a 4xx or 5xx without an error text, and a 2xx other than 200, to :invalid_response, which it documents as a response without the expected shape. sonnet-2's public fetch_forecast/3, haiku-1's private get/3 and haiku-2's private get_forecast/3 name HTTP requests, not key lookups, and are not counted under Naming.
